diagram_math_checks.evidence: The middle horizontal map is exactly Ψ:G_n→Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²), the isomorphism of Statement/L1. The left permutation map has domain G_n and codomain S_n by Statement/L5. The right map is π_Q([f])=π(f), with f(q_j)=q_{π(f)(j)}; L6 and the boundary-fixed mapping-class definition make this constant along representative isotopies, hence well defined. Ordinary composition of homeomorphisms gives the same permutation composition.

Proof step 1.1 gives h_β(q_j)=z_j(1)=q_{π_geo([β])(j)}, so π_Q(Ψ([β]))=π_geo([β]). Thus the lower square with bottom identity S_n→S_n commutes. No inverse is inserted: the inverse monodromy in the original Remarks refers to the distinct covering action convention. The supplier braid-to-mapping-class theorem step 1.2 likewise reads Ψ([β])=[h_β] from the raw slice lift endpoint.

L8 identifies G_n^pure=ker π_geo. L7 and the pure mapping-class definition identify PMod with the subgroup ker π_Q: an isotopy preserving the finite marked set has locally constant permutation, so the pointwise stabilizer injects on components. Step 2.1 establishes the purity equivalence; step 3.1 and bijectivity of Ψ yield the displayed restricted isomorphism. The upper vertical arrows are the two subgroup inclusions, so their square commutes by definition of restriction.

Both local mapping-class definitions use homeomorphisms fixing ∂D² pointwise and ambient isotopies with that condition at every time. Mod preserves Q_n setwise; PMod fixes each marked point. The caption retains precisely these conventions. No boundary rotation, section of π_geo or π_Q, or split extension is drawn or asserted. The diagram works for n=0,1 as well, with trivial S_n.

The entire original file is a byte-identical prefix of the repaired carrier; all additions follow the original final Remarks bullets. Steps 1.1–3.1 prove every relation displayed without invoking the diagram.
